doc.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: His current informal small group and preference over big bands
summary: Prefers loosely organized small groups after eleven years in big bands where he was cast as lead trombonist.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Interesting. How do you feel about your current working band that you have?
Well, this will be the second time we’ve played together. We played one night a couple of weeks ago, just, we’re not very organized.

That’s my favorite kind of music now is when it’s not so organized. But I did that big band thing, I was on the road for eleven years from one band to another, and it’s kind of a freedom to get out and just play with a little small group you know, where you don’t have any real arrangements, maybe an ending now and then or how to start it, but that’s really what I like to do the most now. As a matter of fact I always did but I always got thrown in the lead trombone chair in all these bands, and some of them like Woody’s band I was able to play both lead and jazz solos until Carl Fontana came along, then we had to share the jazz solos.
